issues.body: The `item.completed` branch dispatches on `item["item_type"]`, but Codex JSON item objects use `item["type"]` for values such as `command_execution`, `file_change`, and `agent_message`. Consequently current-protocol tool calls and messages are silently ignored; a real run can be recorded with `probe:0` and no turn evidence despite having inspected the repository. The added fixture is non-representative because it invents `item_type`, so its passing assertion does not validate the actual protocol boundary.
issues.fix_hint: Parse the actual item discriminator (`type`) and replace the fixture with captured/sanitized real `codex exec --json` event shapes. Keep an assertion that fails if real `command_execution` items are not counted.
issues.title: Current Codex item events are read from the wrong discriminator

issues.body: `tool_counts` starts as `{}` and is always written into `usage-telemetry.json`, even if the log is empty, every JSON line is malformed, or the protocol has changed so no recognized telemetry event is parsed. `_no_change_health_envelope` treats any dictionary, including that unconditional empty dictionary, as proof telemetry was measured and emits `probe:0`. This violates the documented and security-relevant absent-versus-zero contract: parser failure or an unknown protocol becomes the strong claim that the model used no inspection tools.
issues.fix_hint: Track whether a recognized harness/protocol event stream was successfully observed and emit `tool_counts` (and therefore `probe`) only when measurement is valid. Fail closed to omission for empty, malformed, mismatched, or wholly unknown streams, and add negative tests for each case.
issues.title: Unknown or malformed telemetry is misreported as a measured zero probes

verdict.summary: The new Codex telemetry path is not sound for the current item protocol and can also turn an unrecognized or malformed event stream into affirmative zero-effort evidence. The tests reproduce the implementation's assumed schema rather than the real wire shape, so they do not catch the primary failure. Because these fields are intended as trust-plane evidence distinguishing an unmeasured run from a measured zero-probe run, both problems are major and must fail closed.
